expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: No, and it fails in the exact scenario that caused this... That lands at rung 2 that fails open. You need Control.

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: It's a check-then-act race (M5). Redelivery fires on visibility-timeout expiry... Both workers SELECT, both find nothing, both charge.

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: An optional idempotency key is rung zero in a costume — implies requirement; key minted at enqueue time in message body

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ON payment_attempts (invoice_id, idempotency_key);

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Defect: 340 customers double-charged, refunded. Mistake: the redelivered message ran the charge path a second time. Hazard: the charge effect is non-idempotent...

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: nothing in the type system or the database says 'at most once per message' — framed as system design property

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: every other consumer on that queue that emails/refunds/provisions/posts to a ledger; every Stripe webhook handler; every retry wrapper; every admin re-run job button

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: Two incidents of one shape means the hazard isn't in the payment worker... The structural move is middleware that reserves the key before dispatching...

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: it's in pairing an at-least-once queue with consumers that mutate the outside world — attributed to system design, not individual
